# What changes does FlashAttention-2 make to the FlashAttention algorithm, and what speedup results?

> **ANSWERED**
> Evidence-sufficiency score 1.00 (heuristic)
> _Uncalibrated: decided by the heuristic scorer, not a fitted model._

## Answer

FlashAttention‑2 revises the original FlashAttention kernel by redesigning how work is divided among GPU threads. *[unverified]* The authors first cut the number of non‑matrix‑multiply floating‑point operations, which had previously consumed a sizable fraction of the compute budget [1]. They then change the partitioning strategy so that the attention computation can be spread across multiple thread blocks even when a single attention head is processed, thereby raising occupancy on the device [1]. Within each block the work is further split among warps, which lessens the amount of data that must pass through shared memory and reduces inter‑warp communication overhead [1]. These modifications directly address the inefficiencies noted in the original design, namely sub‑optimal work distribution between thread blocks and warps that limited performance to only 25‑40 % of the theoretical FLOPs/s ceiling on A100 GPUs [2][3].

The performance impact of the new partitioning is reported as roughly a two‑fold speedup over the prior FlashAttention implementation [1]. *[unverified]* On NVIDIA A100 hardware FlashAttention‑2 attains 50‑73 % of the theoretical maximum FLOPs/s, a substantial jump from the 25‑40 % achieved by the earlier version [1][2][3]. *[unverified]* When integrated end‑to‑end in GPT‑style training, the kernel delivers up to 225 TFLOPs/s per A100 GPU, corresponding to a 72 % utilization of the model’s FLOPs budget [1]. *[unverified]* In contrast, the original FlashAttention already provided a 2‑4× runtime advantage over optimized baselines but remained far from the efficiency of pure GEMM operations [2][3]. *[unverified]* Thus, FlashAttention‑2’s algorithmic tweaks and finer‑grained parallelism translate into a consistent ≈2× acceleration and markedly higher hardware efficiency. *[unverified]*
